ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal federal AML/CFT statute is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), with regulations including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. FINTRAC guidance requires reporting entities to establish beneficial ownership, perform client identification and ongoing monitoring, maintain records, and report suspicious transactions. For a federal corporation, the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, sections 21.1 to 21.303, requires a register of individuals with significant control. For an Alberta corporation, the Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, including the applicable beneficial ownership and corporate-record provisions, must be reviewed together with Alberta Corporate Registry filing requirements. The federal Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Act may apply to residential real estate but does not generally prohibit non-resident ownership of an Alberta operating corporation.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, controllers, and identified beneficial owners before incorporation and before banking. Check United Nations Security Council sanctions, Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, Canadian terrorist listings, FINTRAC and applicable domestic enforcement sources, OFAC SDN and other relevant OFAC lists, UK sanctions where commercially relevant, and politically exposed person and head-of-international-organization databases. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, close associates, family members, high-risk countries, opaque trusts, nominee arrangements, bearer-like control structures, unexplained wealth, adverse media, and high-risk payroll corridors. OFAC screening is not universally mandatory for a Canadian entity but is commercially required where US persons, US dollar clearing, US technology, or US counterparties are involved. Maintain documented false-positive resolution, sanctions escalation, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, transaction monitoring, and suspicious transaction reporting procedures. A Canadian reporting entity must not disclose the filing of a suspicious transaction report to the subject.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, accessed through Alberta.ca and an authorized Alberta registry agent; Alberta corporate name searches generally require a NUANS or equivalent Alberta name-search report where applicable
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An Alberta corporation may use an English, French, or combined English-French corporate name. A corporate name must be distinctive, not misleading, and not confusingly similar to an existing corporate name, business name, trademark, or government entity. A translated or transliterated version may be used only if properly reflected in the articles and accepted by the registry. Non-Latin characters should not be relied upon as the sole legal name for registry, banking, tax, payroll, and payment-rail purposes. The legal corporate name and any assumed business name must be separately documented.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying regulated financial, insurance, securities, immigration, legal, medical, or governmental status without required approval
Names confusingly similar to an existing Alberta corporation, federal corporation, registered business name, trademark, or public authority
Offensive, deceptive, misleading, or otherwise contrary-to-public-policy terms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a current Alberta name-search report and submit the proposed name through an authorized Alberta registry agent with the required articles and supporting consent or approval for sensitive terms. A name reservation or name-search report is not equivalent to trademark clearance. If rejected, obtain the written rejection reason, identify the statutory or similarity basis, and preserve the search report and filing record. Revise the name or provide evidence of consent, distinctiveness, prior rights, or absence of confusion. Request reconsideration from the Alberta registry or the responsible government office through the registry agent. If an adverse administrative decision remains, seek available review or judicial review under Alberta administrative-law procedures, subject to applicable limitation periods. Do not use the rejected name in contracts, payroll, advertising, banking, or immigration documentation pending acceptance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A corporation must maintain a registered office in Alberta and must maintain corporate records and a records office as required by the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A commercial virtual office may be acceptable as a registered office if it is a genuine Alberta address, receives and promptly forwards legal documents, maintains required records or identifies the records office, and satisfies the registry agent and financial institution. A mailbox-only, accommodation-only, or non-operational address is high risk. For a global employer-of-record and cross-border payroll business, a virtual office does not establish operational substance, payroll capability, employment-law compliance, privacy controls, client support, or tax-residency management. The business may require payroll-account registration with the Canada Revenue Agency, workers' compensation registration where applicable, employment-standards compliance, privacy compliance, and additional licensing or registration in the provinces where employees or employment-agency activities occur. Canadian immigration-recruitment services may require use of an authorized immigration representative and provincial recruiter compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 5% to 15% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection at the registered office for an ordinary low-risk corporation, based on the absence of a universal routine inspection program; estimated 15% to 35% during incorporation, banking, payroll, tax, licensing, sanctions, complaint, or enhanced-risk review if the entity has non-resident owners, a virtual office, high-volume cross-border payroll, unusual payment flows, or inconsistent UBO information. These are compliance-risk estimates, not statutory probabilities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, sections 8-10 (incorporation), 21-22 (registered office), 26 (articles), 101-102 (directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Service Alberta, operating the Corporate Registry Information System (CORES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated by the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); shares may be issued for nominal consideration, no escrow account is required, and CAD 10.00 is subscribed as initial paid-up capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the corporation accept the incorporator's subscription and issue 1,000 common shares without par value for aggregate consideration of CAD 10.00, payable in full upon issuance. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office be set at [Registered Office Address] in Alberta, with the named agent for service in accordance with the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole director to hold office until the first annual general meeting. FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Officer Name] be appointed President, Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, with full authority to execute employment agency licensing, payroll vendor agreements, banking resolutions, and all statutory post-incorporation filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) – Name Approval / NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS/Corporate Registry name search through a corporate registrant or directly via CORES. Submit a Name Reservation Request specifying the proposed corporate name. If the name is approved, the reservation is valid for 90 days. Ensure the name contains a legal element ('Inc.,' 'Corp.,' 'Ltd.') and is not confusingly similar to existing Alberta/federal names.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporate name structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended Name Reservation Request with an alternate name; objection may be cured by adding differentiating distinctive words or obtaining consent from the existing name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator / legal counsel; filed with Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) stating share structure, registered office, and director restrictions, complete director consent forms, and have the incorporator/initial director sign. Notarization is not generally required for domestic entities; verify signatory identity when filing electronically through CORES.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director – initial director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registry returns a defect, file a corrected Form 1 with the statutory correction procedure within 30 days or re-file as an amended incorporation application; use the Registry's deficiency notice to amend wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) online portal / authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed articles and consents into CORES, pay the prescribed filing fee by corporate credit card or registered account. The system will generate a transaction number; a PDF acknowledgment is available immediately. Retain the submission receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for validation errors, use the CORES resubmission queue and correct the data elements identified; make a new payment only if the original transaction was not accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following registry review, the Registrar of Corporations issues a Certificate of Incorporation with a corporate number and effective date. The certificate authorizes the corporation to carry on business as a legal entity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond SLA, submit a status inquiry through CORES or Service Alberta contact center; if certificate contains data errors, apply for a correction under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors; Alberta Employment Standards Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma resolution, issue share certificates, fix registered office/agent, execute officer resolutions, open a corporate bank account, and apply for the Employment Agency Licence and municipal business permits before commencing EOR payroll operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If employment licence application is queried, respond to Alberta Employment Standards Branch with corrected staffing agreements, proof of workers' compensation registration, and updated corporate disclosure within the stated deficiency period.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (registration only) – administrative office use; no specified major industrial activity under the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act; if later operating a physical employment training facility, a Preliminary Assessment would be required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent; administrative office operation must comply with municipal stormwater and wastewater discharge bylaws (e.g., City of Calgary Sewer Use Bylaw), Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for any HVAC-related combustion emissions, and federal VOC limits under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act if solvents/cleaners are used.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), the federal tax authority responsible for administering income tax, GST/HST, and related obligations, with the primary portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian corporations receive a Business Number (BN) upon incorporation through the Alberta provincial registry and subsequent CRA enrollment for tax identification and filing obligations. Foreign entities must register separately if carrying on business in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective mechanisms available under Canadian tax law. Corporate classification is statutory, with no hybrid mismatch elections permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies triggering mandatory GST registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, digital stamping, or fiscal clearance system required for GST. Registrants must file periodic GST/HST returns via the CRA My Business portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST rate applies to exports of goods or zero-rated supplies of services when the goods are exported from Canada or the services are performed outside Canada and satisfy the conditions of the Excise Tax Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits GST zero-rating claims; fraudulent claims result in assessment of tax due plus penalties up to 200% of the tax, interest, and potential criminal prosecution. Retrospective clawbacks apply for improper claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - the monetary authority and foreign-exchange agent for the Government of Canada; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator of Schedule I chartered banks under the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46); the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/ATF supervisor under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); and Global Affairs Canada as administrator of economic sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act. Canada's exchange liberalization derives from the Currency Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-52) and the repeal of the former Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible. Canada has assumed Article VIII obligations of the IMF Articles of Agreement, so current-account payments, capital-account transfers, dividend remittances and intercompany funding are not subject to exchange-control approvals or quantitative limits. The exchange rate floats freely under the Bank of Canada's inflation-control mandate. The only substantial remittance hurdle is tax-driven, not currency-driven: non-resident profit and dividend remittances carry Part XIII withholding tax of 25% statutory, typically reduced to 15% or 5% under the Canada-US Convention (5% for a US parent holding at least 10% of voting power) and comparable treaties; interest paid to non-resident shareholders or creditors is subject to a 25% base withholding and to 10% or 15% treaty rates. Such taxes are withholding obligations, not repatriation duties, and do not restrict convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no repatriation deadline for export or services proceeds; a Canadian EOR entity may retain 100% of foreign-currency receivables in CAD or in any convertible currency. Operative compliance constraints are limited to: (a) FINTRAC international EFT reporting for each inbound or outbound wire of CAD 10,000 or more (due within five business days); (b) sanctions and export-control screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act (the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and Public Safety Canada's sanctions database); and (c) Income Tax Act section 247 transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany service revenue. There is no legal obligation to convert export receipts to CAD.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech rails are rated High for disbursement-side treasury (Wise, certified as a foreign MSB registered with FINTRAC, and Payoneer) and Medium-to-Low for legal-entity cash concentration. Canadian-dollar clearing requires a FINTRAC-registered MSB, and the incoming Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), supervised by the Bank of Canada, will require payment service providers to obtain authorization and to safeguard client funds; an offshore digital EMI without MSB or PSP registration cannot lawfully clear payroll in Canada. Wise balances are not CDIC-insured and are not deposits in a Schedule I bank, so a prudent structure uses a Schedule I bank for capital escrow and operational concentration, with Wise or Payoneer batch APIs only for small-value, high-frequency contractor payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal statutory in-person mandate exists under the PCMLTFA; section 70 of the PCMLTFA Regulations permits non-face-to-face onboarding if enhanced KYC steps are completed. In practice, Schedule I banks require at least one signing director or authorized officer to attend an in-person interview at the Calgary or Edmonton commercial banking centre when the account will process high-volume payroll; for capital-escrow or trust-like accounts, physical attendance is close to mandatory. Remote opening is possible for a Canadian-controlled corporation with digital verification (Alberta corporate registry extract, live video ID, corporate resolution and notarized passport), but account limits and product approvals are typically reduced. Recommended posture: arrange an in-person interview at the commercial centre where the account is domiciled and appoint a named treasury officer as the principal signing authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EOR pay-through profile: high aggregate account turnover, thin net margin, frequent third-party disbursements and insufficient end-client documentation, triggering reclassification as an unregistered money-services business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master EOR service agreements with end-clients; attested payroll registers and client funding schedules; CRA payroll account number with T4/T4A remittance vouchers; Alberta WCB (Workers' Compensation Board) certificate of eligibility for the staffing licence; board resolutions authorizing the disbursement matrix; a written Letter of Assurance confirming the entity is not conducting money-services business without FINTRAC registration; audited financial statements for the first operating year.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity international EFTs to a diverse set of foreign contractor beneficiaries, with individual wires at or near the CAD 10,000 FINTRAC international-EFT reporting threshold, creating FINTRAC suspicious-transaction reporting considerations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed contractor agreements and underlying invoices; per-beneficiary sanctions screening results against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and the US OFAC SDN list; tax-residency declarations (W-8BEN for US contractors, NR6/NR4 documentation for Canadian-resident contractors, and equivalent forms for other jurisdictions); detailed payroll instruction archive; a controlled disbursement schedule; confirmation letters that no funds are received from third parties outside the contractual EOR chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership or foreign directors without a clear Canadian nexus; presence of nominee directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Status; register of directors and ultimate beneficial owners prepared under the Alberta Business Corporations Act or Canada Business Corporations Act; full UBO chain diagram; passport and foreign tax identification numbers of all 25% or greater beneficiaries; proof of Canadian permanent residence or work authorization for the administrator; PEP/SIP declarations; financial forecasting statements and closing balance-sheet evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent or venture fund where loan-versus-equity is ambiguous, raising money-laundering and thin-capitalization concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement; source-of-funds statements covering the entire funding chain; board resolution approving the injection; tax opinion confirming section 15(2) and 80.4 deemed-benefit analysis and thin-capitalization compliance (debt-to-equity ratio of 1.5:1 for foreign-controlled entities under section 18(4)); contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation under section 247; filing proof for Part XIII withholding (NR4) where interest or dividends are distributed; completed bank AML and onboarding questionnaire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection: SWIFT MT103 with remittance field 70 'Share subscription - [Corporate name], [Alberta Corporate Access Number]', accompanied by (i) board resolution, (ii) private placement exemption memo, and (iii) updated share-allotment filing at the Alberta Corporate Registry; beneficiary bank SWIFT codes: RBC ROYCCAT2, TD TDOMCATTTOR, BMO BOFMCAM2, CIBC CIBCCATT, Scotiabank NOSCCATT, ATB ATBTCATM. Shareholder loan injection: field 70 must cite the loan agreement date and loan character, e.g. '[date] shareholder loan - non-arm's-length funding'; file T106 transfer-pricing disclosure where applicable; register NR4 and remit Part XIII withholding on interest paid to foreign lenders; and maintain the 1.5:1 thin-capitalization limit for foreign-controlled entities. Domestic CAD funding moves via Lynx (RTGS) for same-day settlement; every international wire of CAD 10,000 or more triggers a FINTRAC international-EFT report within five business days, and the receiving bank will require a declaration of the source of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic contractor payroll: CAD direct deposits cleared through the ACSS via the bank's payroll EFT file referenced to the CRA payroll account, with the upcoming Real-Time Rail (RTR) available for instant payroll continuity once Payments Canada finalizes deployment. Cross-border contractor payments: (a) SWIFT MT103 in serial or cover method with field 70 narrative 'cross-border contractor services remuneration' for individual wires above the economic threshold; (b) Wise or Payoneer batch API rails for small-value, high-frequency disbursements to contractors denominated in USD, EUR, GBP and other liquid currencies; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit are not a natural rail for pure EOR service remuneration because services lack transferable title documents, but standby LCs (UCP600/ISP98) and advance-payment guarantees are permissible for client-fixed project pre-funding and escrow structures. All outbound international EFTs at or above CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC within five business days; fund transfers to sanctioned jurisdictions are prohibited under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's standard forward terms, supported by a hedge designation memorandum mapping each forward to the underlying EOR payroll liability.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore-traded emerging-market currencies (e.g., BRL, INR, PHP, VND) where the underlying payroll invoice is denominated in a restricted currency and the NDF is documented as an economic hedge under ASPE 3856 or IFRS 9 hedge documentation.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-dated multi-currency contractor-liability structures, executed with OSFI-regulated Schedule I counterparties and, where applicable, cleared through the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC).
Short-dated FX swaps and tom-next rollovers to reposition liquidity between the CAD operating account and foreign-currency settlement accounts on payroll funding dates.

Foreign-exchange option collars (zero-premium range forwards) on the invoice portfolio, permissible under a board-approved treasury and derivatives policy, with tax characterization of ordinary income confirmed by Canadian tax counsel.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return of a Corporation (ABCA annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the corporation's incorporation, not its fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty plus loss of certificate-of-compliance status; after two consecutive default years the Registrar may strike the corporation from the register and initiate administrative dissolution; reinstatement requires director or court restoration and higher fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate tax administered by CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, under the Canada-Alberta tax collection agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end for the T2 return; unpaid balance generally due two months after fiscal year-end, and three months for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small business deduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeated-filing penalty may reach 10% plus 2% per month up to 20%; daily compound interest accrues; directors may incur personal liability for unremitted payroll and withholding amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Alberta Business Corporations Act imposes no revenue or asset audit threshold for private corporations. An independent auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, have consented to waive the auditor requirement; distributing or publicly listed corporations cannot waive. The CRA or another competent regulator may also demand audited financial statements in appropriate circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises and distributing corporations apply International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS, CPA Canada Handbook Part I); non-distributing private corporations may apply Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II). The EOR business must maintain adequate payroll, payroll-tax, and employment-records accounting reconciling gross payroll, statutory deductions, employer contributions, and remittances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual Return requires confirmation of officers, directors, and registered office but not a separate UBO schedule. Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the corporation must maintain an individuals-with-significant-control register and update it within 15 days after any share transfer creating or terminating significant control; a share transfer should also be recorded in the Register of Transfers and approved in board or shareholder minutes. Recommended annual process: reconcile share ledgers, transfer register, director consents, ISC register, and minute book before filing the Annual Return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book (shareholder meetings, director meetings, resolutions and written consents)
Registered office address record and records-of-resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500–12,000 per year for a small-to-mid-size EOR or payroll entity; lower if audit is waived and only review or compilation financials are prepared

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% general combined (15% federal + 8% Alberta); 11% combined on first CAD 500,000 active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (9% federal + 2% Alberta)
